target_customer: Real estate agents, property marketers, facilities and construction teams that need 3D models of spaces
problem: Capturing an accurate 3D model of a building interior required expensive scanners. Matterport built a cheap camera plus cloud software that turns scans into navigable 3D models.
business_model: Hardware camera sales plus SaaS subscriptions and per space processing

founders.name: David Gausebeck
founders.background_notes: The only founder listed on the YC page; other founders not verified in this pass.

technical_complexity.rationale: Required a custom depth camera built on PrimeSense sensors plus computer vision to stitch scans into 3D models, a hardware and research heavy problem for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Proprietary camera, processing pipeline and a growing library of captured spaces were hard to copy quickly, though 360 cameras later lowered the barrier.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Autodesk had photo based 123D Catch; Zillow later added a free 3D home tool. None displaced Matterport, and CoStar bought it in 2025.

market_need_then: Real estate, insurance and home improvement listings lacked cheap 3D capture; the CEO aimed to be the go to brand when 3D imaging became standard in those markets.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioning moved from virtual tours to digital twins

branding.brand_signature: Matterport as shorthand for 3D tours of spaces, with product names like Showcase and Space

rebrands.why: Shift in vision to digitize and index the built world; a new matterport.com launched, per a forum source

branding.community_and_virality: Large community forums of 3D tour providers discuss Matterport, including a thread debating a more searchable product name.

brand_strength.rationale: Known within real estate imaging and a Nasdaq listed brand, but evidence comes from forums and aggregators, not brand studies.

outcome_analysis: Matterport built proprietary hardware and cloud software for 3D capture, raised about 56M by 2015 from Qualcomm Ventures, DCM and others, listed through a SPAC in July 2021, then agreed to a roughly 1.6B sale to CoStar completed in February 2025. It grew as the leader in its niche, though the premium paid shows a stock that lagged earlier hopes.
notes: Directory status is Public; exit recorded as the later CoStar acquisition completed 2025-02, after a SPAC listing on 2021-07-22 (merger closed per a forum source; sponsor name not verified). Series A amount conflicts: 4M, 5.6M or 7.4M; recorded as null. A 5M Ericsson round in 2017 and a 48M round headline in 2019 are single source and not recorded. One source says the CoStar price was 2.1B, others 1.6B. Founding year not stated on the YC page. No dated 2012 competitor source found, so the list is empty; the 123D Catch mention is undated. Founders beyond Gausebeck not verified.
